title: introduce-cost-janitor-prefill-policy-and-quant-hinting
author: Sofia Alvarez
release_notes: Adds a background ‘Cost Janitor’ service that applies workload-derived prefill and quantization hints to reduce unit costs while preserving latency SLOs. Tunable via Redwood Console and disabled-by-default for existing clusters.
description:
Summary: Introduces 'Cost Janitor', a lightweight controller that synthesizes workload signals (prefix hit rates, request sparsity, and latency percentiles) into safe default prefill policies and quantization hints for model variants. The controller emits recommendations, can apply non-breaking config seeds to Dedicated/Private clusters, and exposes audit events for all changes. Motivation: Many customers underutilize prefill and conservative quantization defaults, leaving 10-30% unit-economy on the table. This PR provides an automated, auditable path to surface and optionally apply low-risk adjustments so teams can safely converge to better cost/latency tradeoffs.

What changed (high level):
- New component: services/cost_janitor (controller + reconciler + lightweight ML heuristic library)
- API: /v1/admin/cost-jobs (create/list/react) and console hooks to preview recommendations
- Runtime: new prefill_policy hint metadata on model variants; quant_hint profile metadata for quantization tiers
- Telemetry: audit events, recommendation traces, and a new metric redwood_cost_janitor_recommendation{result}
- Tests: unit tests for heuristics + an integration smoketest that runs controller against a local dev workload sample

Commits (high level):
- 0a7c3d1: initial controller scaffolding, CRD-like config and scheduler
- 2f9b1aa: heuristics: prefix-hit decay, tail-latency guard, cold-prefill threshold
- 5d4a2b8: API endpoints and console preview payloads
- 7f6e8c4: telemetry and audit event wiring; add metrics and tracing spans
- 9b1f3e0: tests and CI flake fix (retries for smoketest)

Files changed (not exhaustive):
- services/cost_janitor/controller.go (new)
- services/cost_janitor/heuristics.go (new)
- api/admin/cost_jobs.go (new endpoints)
- models/variant_metadata.go (adds PrefillPolicy & QuantHint fields)
- console/src/components/CostJanitorPreview.tsx (console preview UI)
- metrics/metrics_defs.yaml (new metric)
- tests/cost_janitor_smoketest.sh (integration smoke test)

Design notes and safety:
- Recommendations are tagged with a safety score (0-1). Only scores >= 0.75 are auto-applied when 'auto_apply' is enabled for a cluster.
- Janitor never lowers model precision on variants that are pinned or marked 'no-auto-quant'.
- Prefill policy changes begin as shadow/apply-preview by default; customers must opt into auto-apply.
- All changes generate audit logs and offer a 24h rollback window (configurable per cluster).

Performance and cost expectations:
- Internal benchmarking on three sample workloads showed 8-18% reduction in token cost for conversational traffic and 4-9% for single-turn generation without SLO regression.
- Benchmarks were run on p4d and a16 hardware; results are included in the PR artifact (benchmarks/README.md).

CI and validation:
- CI run summary: build ✓, unit tests ✓, lint ✓, integration-smoketest initially failed (timeout on smoketest step), retried and passed on rerun. Full CI attached in checks panel.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ethan Clarke (reviewer): "This looks promising. Two concerns: 1) semantic tests around quant hints — how do we validate output quality? 2) metrics cardinality if we emit per-variant recommendation traces?"
- Author (Sofia): "Added a small qual-check harness that runs a delta-bleu/embedding-similarity test on a 100-example QA set for any candidate quant hint. It is lightweight and only runs in prerelease mode. For metrics, we aggregate by model_family + cluster to avoid high cardinality; per-variant traces are sampled (1%)."
- Priya Nair: "Would like a knob in Console to preview cumulative delta on cost and p95 before applying — is that possible?"
- Sofia: "Console preview now shows an estimated cost delta and p95 impact based on historical samples. See console preview UI changes and backend budget estimator in heuristics.go."
- Jordan Li: "Nit: rename 'auto_apply' in config to 'apply_mode' with explicit enum (disabled, preview, auto). Also prefer the default to be 'preview' for safety."
- Sofia: "Addressed: config renamed, default set to 'preview', tests updated."

Manual testing and rollout:
- Deployed to staging Dedicated cluster (staging-dedicated-03) for 72h with auto_apply=preview and sampled traffic. Observed expected reduction in inferred unit cost and no p95 SLA violations.
- Runbook updated: docs/runbooks/cost_janitor.md with steps to audit, roll back, and tune thresholds.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge
- Merge commit: "Introduce Cost Janitor controller, admin API, and console preview"

Follow-ups / TODOs (tracked in Linear):
- ENG-1304: Add drift detection that re-evaluates recommendations weekly
- ENG-1317: Add experiment channel to run A/B application of recommended prefill policies
- ENG-1350: Add richer qual checks (LLM-specific evals) to the quant hint pipeline

Why this is different from previous econ PRs: Cost Janitor emphasizes small, auditable, incremental changes surfaced as recommendations first (preview path) with a focus on safe auto-apply gating. It blends low-cost heuristics with lightweight qual checks and conservative rollout mechanics rather than a fully automatic autotuner. This lowers risk for customers who want gradual cost improvements and clear rollback paths.
